title: Polanski heckled at Jewish community hustings after saying that Zionism is a form of racism – UK politics live
summary:
The Green leader, who is Jewish, made the remarks as part of his campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection

Morning, and welcome to our UK politics live blog.

Zack…

image.caption: Leader of the Green party of England and Wales, Zack Polanski Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA

blocks.text: Polanski heckled as he declares himself an anti-Zionist at byelection hustings
Morning, and welcome to our UK politics live blog.

Zack Polanski declared himself an anti-Zionist and faced heckling at a Jewish community hustings in Holborn and St Pancras, where the Green party leader is standing as a candidate in next month’s byelection.

He said Zionism – the movement for a Jewish state – was a form of racism because it involved the displacement and genocide of Palestinians. His remarks were met with boos from the audience last night.

blocks.caption: Zack Polanski said he was an anti-Zionist during a by-election hustings event at a Jewish community centre in Holborn and St Pancras. Photograph: Aldo Ciarrocchi/Alamy

blocks.text: “I’m an anti-Zionist. I think countries have always been ideas and I think things change over time,” he said.

Polanski, who is Jewish, said criticising the Israeli government and the occupation of Palestinian land was not antisemitic. “We need to come together to recognise that when we call that antisemitic, we are making ourselves as Jewish people less safe,” he added.

As the Green party prepares for its annual conference, members are due to vote on a motion to declare Zionism as a form of racism in official policy. As my colleague Peter Walker reported last week, some in the party fear it could alienate Jewish supporters if it passed:

double quotation markA Green official said that many activists loyal to the party’s leadership might not be at the autumn conference because it takes place a week before voting in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection, in which Polanski hopes to take Keir Starmer’s old seat from Labour, potentially leaving more scope for others to push through the motion. “The risk is that if it passes as it is we are alienating ourselves from the Jewish community in the UK, a lot of whom are not big fans of the current Israeli government,” a Green source said. There was, they added, a parallel worry about internal splits, with some Green activists in leaked WhatsApp chats warning that Polanski was “struggling to overcome Zionist indoctrination”.
